newsitem.title: GERMANY: Focus - Veba optimistic after good 97 start.
newsitem.headline: Focus - Veba optimistic after good 97 start.

text.p: German energy and telecommunications group Veba AG said on Tuesday it expected to increase its profits this year after an unexpectedly good first quarter and amid continued efforts to cut costs.
In a statement which sent its share price surging, Veba reported a seven percent rise in first quarter net profit to 486 million marks and an eight percent increase in sales.

Growth was driven by "significant" earnings and sales advances in its oil business and its trading, transport and services division, although chemical sector business was hampered by high raw materials costs, Veba said.

"Because of the overall positive development of the first quarter and despite the difficult start in the chemical sector we are confident of being able to raise earnings again for the full year of 1997," the company said.
Veba reported net profits of 2.63 billion marks for 1996, an increase of 25 percent, but warned in March that earnings growth would slow this year.
The utility group's shares surged on the news, which dealers said was sharply above most forecasts.
After hitting an early high of 94.02 marks, Veba retained most of its early gains to trade up 3.45 marks, or 3.8 percent, at 93.55 marks in the bourse session.
The blue chip DAX index was up one percent.
Veba said higher profits from its oil and trading, transport, and service segments more than compensated for a "significant earnings decrease" in chemicals.
The company also said its telecommunications interests, still in their build-up phase, ended the period at a loss "according to plan."
"Continued measures to cut costs and raise efficiency as well as further optimisation of (our) portfolio will also contribute to the earnings improvement," Veba said.
Sales in the first quarter rose 7.8 percent to 19.624 billion marks, with oil sales showing the biggest advance to rise 19.1 percent to 4.925 billion marks.
In the chemicals sector, sales dropped by 1.6 percent to 2.6 billion marks.
